description: Multi-trait genomic BLUP (GBLUP) on 3000 wheat lines × 20000 SNPs; dominant cost is the 3000×3000 genomic relationship matrix built inside the tool via numpy BLAS.
prompt: Fit a multi-trait genomic prediction model (GBLUP) for a synthetic wheat breeding program. First generate the dataset with numpy seed 0: (1) genotype matrix M of shape 3000×20000 where each entry is sampled from {0, 1, 2} with probabilities [0.09, 0.42, 0.49] (HWE frequencies at minor allele frequency 0.3). (2) Simulate two correlated quantitative traits — grain yield (GY) and grain protein content (GPC) — under the additive infinitesimal model. IMPORTANT: do NOT sample any high-dimensional multivariate normal (never build a 3000×3000 or larger covariance and draw from it — that is numerically unstable). Instead, work at the marker level: draw a 20000×2 matrix of per-SNP allele-substitution effects by sampling standard normals and applying the 2×2 Cholesky factor of the genetic-correlation matrix [[1, rg], [rg, 1]] with rg=-0.40 (so the two traits' SNP effects are correlated at rg); center the genotype columns to get M_c; compute each trait's true genetic value g = M_c @ beta_trait (a 3000×20000 by 20000 matmul); then standardize g to unit variance and form phenotypes y = g*sqrt(h2) + e where e ~ N(0, 1-h2) drawn elementwise per line, using h²_GY=0.45 and h²_GPC=0.30. (3) a fixed-effects matrix with 3000 rows encoding an environment covariate (0 or 1, alternating every 100 lines) plus an intercept column. Call fit_genomic_prediction_model from biomni.tool.genetics with model_type='additive' — this builds the 3000×3000 genomic relationship matrix from the 3000×20000 genotypes and solves the mixed-model equations (the dominant compute). Report: (a) estimated heritability for each trait, (b) top 10 SNP indices by absolute effect size for GY, (c) 5-fold cross-validated prediction accuracy as Pearson r between predicted GEBVs and phenotypes for both traits.
notes: Calls biomni.tool.genetics.fit_genomic_prediction_model (numpy/scipy/torch — portable to MN5). Dominant compute is the 3000×3000 genomic relationship matrix G = (1/m)*M_c @ M_c.T built INSIDE the tool from the 3000×20000 genotypes (~1.8e11 FLOPs) plus the per-trait mixed-model solve; 5-fold CV repeats it ~5×. SEGFAULT FIX (2026-08-04): the previous prompt said 'draw polygenic effects from a multivariate normal with covariance proportional to G' — the agent built a 6000×6000 covariance (2×2 trait ⊗ 3000×3000 G) and called np.random.multivariate_normal, whose eigendecomposition SIGSEGV'd MN5's BLAS (rc=139, no trace written; it had completed on du04 via a lighter random code path). Prompt now mandates the standard marker-effect infinitesimal model (cheap per-SNP 2×2 draw, then M_c @ beta) — no large-dimensional Gaussian. NEEDS RE-TEST after this fix. Note: first MN5 sweep showed the other real-tool tasks are generate-dominated (execute 7-63s vs generate 120-260s, bubble 5-21%) — expect this task similar once it runs, not the 60-80% originally guessed (that guess was from the fake gsea-style single-turn heavy-CPU pattern).
